**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/runtime/config (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/config-resolution.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

- `content/docs/releases/v14.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /api/settings (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-settings/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b93e35824eedd73920d35d54070f88703e4846cc` — the merge of head `e6522a9572fade10de53501faca4758190ae9b57` into base `6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b93e35824eedd73920d35d54070f88703e4846cc && git checkout b93e35824eedd73920d35d54070f88703e4846cc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2 e6522a9572fade10de53501faca4758190ae9b57 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2 && git merge --no-ff e6522a9572fade10de53501faca4758190ae9b57

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6440cf16334e1c8106dfdb31d87b6ca728d176c2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The delivered half matches the ruling:
- Under `single`, runtime-config reads `branding.workspace_name` / `logo_url` / `accent_color` per request. A key nobody set falls back to the deployment's own branding.
- `theme_mode` and `support_email` retire through the version step, refused `400 UNKNOWN_KEY` by name, so the 「甲」 fallback is not needed.

Accepted deviations:
- the host option grouped with the env vars as the deployment default;
- `accent_color`'s unserved default dropped;
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the precedent of #21970.

The seat's answers to the three open questions are its implementation calls, not product questions:

1. **The Setup entry moves with the capability (the dev's option A), in this PR.**
   - `SettingsServicePlugin` contributes the one `nav_settings_branding` item from the `kernel:ready` step that already offers the namespace, the in-tree `connect-ui` pattern.
   - `SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS` drops the line.
   - `check-app-nav-i18n.mjs`'s contributor roster keeps the moved id in that gate's population.
   - Labels stay keyed `apps.setup.navigation.nav_settings_branding`.
   - Cross-lane, declared in the claim: `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts` (one line, `domain:engine`) and `packages/cli/scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` (one roster entry, `domain:cli`).
   - **Pins:** the entry under `single`, and its absence under `group`.
2. **The walled-boot warn goes (option A).**
   - `plugin-auth`'s `branding.workspace_name` binding is skipped when the settings service does not list the `branding` namespace, the same test the runtime-config door makes. A walled boot logs nothing about it.
   - Claim surface: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`, the `applyBrand` binding only.
   - PR #24931 (in the merge queue) edits another region of the same file; whichever lands second merges `main`.
   - **Pin:** a walled boot emits no `warn` for it, and `single` still applies a saved name.
3. **The first line.** After this round the seat rewrites it to `Fixes #24766`, and the dev does not edit the body. The dev's out-of-scope notes stay notes; the QA checklist step wording goes to the Acceptance notes.

Before ACCEPT the seat owes a contract-review-tier review of the narrowing: the settings accept set, and the namespace withheld under a wall.
